identity.name: Eichi II Spring Drive
identity.one_liner: Credor's hand-finished Spring Drive with a hand-painted porcelain dial — a high-end Seiko sub-brand, not Grand Seiko, the quietest haute horlogerie from a Japanese company.

provenance_events.description: Credor (Seiko's hand-finished sub-brand) releases the Eichi II with a 7R14 hand-wound Spring Drive movement and a hand-painted Arita porcelain dial, in a 39mm white-gold case.

narrative.story: Credor is the in-house hand-finished line within the Seiko group. The Eichi II is Credor's most-photographed piece: a 39mm white-gold case, a hand-painted Arita porcelain dial with a single Arabic "12" numeral, and a 7R14 hand-wound Spring Drive movement.
narrative.collector_notes: The Arita porcelain dial is hand-painted by a single artisan — each dial is a one-off work. The power-reserve indicator wanders across the dial in 60 minutes, like a slow minute hand.
